YOLO-1ui.2, classify local communication authority. Five branches resolved in dependency order: name the missing term -> resolve the THREAT-MODEL self-contradiction -> localhost TCP policy -> LM Studio access path -> Unix socket policy. Exploration did the heavy lifting and repeatedly beat asking: a live listener/socket inventory produced the decisive examples (Discord RPC as uncredentialed authority; ~/.config/iterm2/sockets/secrets reachable straight through filesystem.denyRead, which validated the term we had just written); reading domain-pattern.js proved matchesDomainPattern never inspects the port, which killed the obvious mechanism and forced address-level separation; reading macos-sandbox-utils.js showed allowUnixSockets compiles to a Seatbelt subpath prefix, which solved the per-project .beads/bd.sock problem in one entry. Surfaced a real contradiction between THREAT-MODEL's Accepted Tradeoffs table and its own qualification gate, and diagnosed the table's rationale as a category error (it argues about exfiltrating files, not about acting as the developer). One user answer -- 'i want agents to use lmstudio' -- overturned my recommendation to deny loopback outright and produced a better option than any I had listed. CONTEXT.md updated inline the moment the term resolved and kept implementation-free; ADR 0001 created because all three tests held (host provisioning is costly to reverse, a future reader would absolutely wonder why 127.0.0.2 appears and 127.0.0.1 does not, and three genuine alternatives were weighed). Implementation deliberately split to YOLO-fyy, including an explicit instruction to prove the SRT proxies survive losing localhost before relying on the approach.

Resale-catalog data-model pass, thrifting-clothing project. Seven branches resolved in dependency order: seen-vs-verdict relationship -> swipe/review-deck fate -> scope of seller posted/bumped dates -> where price/heat monitoring should live -> check_alive queue priority -> price_history write threshold -> heat UI surfacing. Grounded every question in actual code before asking (db.py, ingest.py, restock.py, scrape_search.py, check_alive.py, backfill_sizes.py, index.html) rather than asking generically; this surfaced that check_alive.py already visits every listing individually but discards the page load after one regex match -- the decisive fact that reframed the whole session from "do we scrape a new date field" into "extend the sweep we already pay for." A user correction mid-session (parallel-scan-then-click, not Tinder-style one-by-one judging) killed the swipe/review deck outright and reframed Seen as click-derived rather than a manual toggle. Caught a real glossary collision between the pre-existing term Demand signal (retrospective, brand-level, from sold_log) and the new concept Heat (live, listing-level, forward-looking) and got it confirmed via a wait-what sub-dialogue with concrete before/after examples. CONTEXT.md created lazily and updated inline as each term resolved, kept implementation-free; one ADR opened only once all three tests held (check_alive.py absorbing price/heat duties is costly to reverse, breaks its own documented stalest-first ordering in a way a future reader would question, and had a genuine rejected alternative -- a separate watcher -- for a specific cost reason). Explicitly scoped an adjacent bug (unsized listings from a title-parsing regex gap) OUT of the pass rather than absorbing it, since it was a data-quality bug, not a data-model question.
